requirements.text: Seats: long- and short-lived, state card, template copy then tune, seat management page with worker activity, user layer vs lead layer.
Instances and the instance page: per-instance home, login state, version and new-version notice without auto-upgrade, concurrency; no quota integration in v1.
Sessions are cache, seat ledger is the sole authority; restart reconciliation; native resume/fork only as equivalent optimisations.
Side chat window: fork lead context by ledger position, batched sync, on-demand read of this project's threads, keep/archive/delete, may write within its permission tier.
Inbox: queue, steer, cancel, edit; interrupt-and-resume fallback disclosed.
Secretary as a global seat: real-time read of all projects' threads, delivery to leads and auditors, resident and scheduled triggers, per-project filtering on distribution.
Lead orchestrates subordinate seats inside user-set bounds; cannot change its own instance; no recursive seat creation; parallel cap from machine resources.
Isolated write spaces; permission tiers enforced by the host with the mechanisms actually available, stated honestly; main tree written only through merge by a permitted seat.
Five CLIs in v1: Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, each with a pinned version and an honest capability report.
Configurable call-permission table enforced by the host; forged or unauthorised senders rejected; subordinate seats cannot reach the Owner.
Gate and stage primitives: approve or reject with reason, reject cap then escalate, user-defined stages, configured gates cannot be bypassed, every transition recorded.
Configurable escalation chain executed by the host; stuck or stalled seats escalate automatically.
Formal review sessions are zero-inheritance; Owner side-chat talk never enters delegated review; workers cannot see Owner-lead conversation.
Global context and memory are unreachable from project-scope retrieval; distribution into a project is explicit, filtered and cited.
Every question to the Owner carries proposed solutions and a free answer; vendor-native question cards shown as-is, otherwise ours; answers are bound back to the asking turn.
Lead answers the takeover questions, including how the project space works, before it may dispatch; each answer cites a source or says unknown and how to find out.
All worktrees created by the host under one standard outside the repository; single and mixed trees stored apart; relations kept as a graph; vendor-native worktree creation not used.
Each instance has its own home, separate from the Owner's everyday CLI homes, with vendor memory turned off; explicit child environment.
Health signals drive automatic compaction and session renewal with a low-key record; instance changes stay explicit.
A repository may serve several projects; commits carry project, seat, instance and turn identity; push credentials are never read or copied by the host.
Cross-line contracts are frozen before parallel work; fakes and real implementations pass the same contract tests; stored records stay readable across schema changes.
Queued: steer, edit, cancel; recipient never changes on focus change.
Steering: shows inserting; never delivered without a receipt.
Steer hit turn end: stays queued or cancel; never silently moved to the next turn or another seat.
Delivered: time shown, interrupt-and-resume disclosed; no recall or edit.
Delivery unknown: read-only check, no automatic resend.
Cancelled: struck through, record kept.
Failed: requeue creates a new message and keeps the old one.
Idle: dispatch, change instance, reclaim, short to long; lead only touches lead-layer seats inside bounds.
Working: inbox and steer, request stop; no instance change while busy.
Switching instance: reason shown; never dispatch to old and new sessions at once.
Stop requested: shown until the stop fact arrives; no new work into an overlapping workspace before it, including leftover child processes and restarts.
Stuck or stalled: escalates along the configured chain; no Owner popup unless the chain reaches the Owner.
Reclaiming: the lead's own reclaim conditions are checked; reclaim refused when unmet.
Reclaimed: greyed out, ledger kept and readable.
New side chat: seat and instance chosen, ledger position and permission tier shown; no model call before the first question.
Active: ask, read this project's threads, inbox operations, writes only within the permission tier; never another project; synced content never executed.
Lead progressed: pending deltas shown and attached to the next question, or appended where the vendor supports append without a turn; no model call for syncing.
Kept by default: resumable; forked lead context not duplicated.
Archived: restore or delete.
Deleted: only the side chat's own content removed; lead ledger unchanged.
Not installed: install guidance for the pinned version.
Installed, not logged in: the Owner logs in inside the CLI; the host never reads or copies credential files.
Logged in: concurrency cap set and enforced; seats served are listed; quota view not in v1.
New version: shown, upgraded only by the Owner's manual action.
Exhausted or error, sourced from the CLI's own error in v1: reason and affected seats shown; no silent instance change.

shared_files.rule: Only the integrator seat writes these files. L0 opens the minimal extension point each line needs before that line starts; later changes go through a change request that names the requesting line, the contract affected and the dependent lines notified.

shared_files.conditional_rule: A conditional file is recorded in T00 or L0 as either MODIFIED, with the change, or VERIFIED_UNCHANGED, with the reason; no line widens its own scope to reach it.

contracts.rule: Frozen in L0. Each operation fixes request and receipt, trusted caller, permission and version checks, state transitions, idempotency, race and recovery semantics, and which store owns the durable state. Fakes and real implementations run the same contract tests. real_stage is the milestone at which the real implementation is settled; every contract is settled again on the candidate at M3. Changing a frozen contract is a change request.

operations.seams: B emits vendor-raw events tagged with session; A normalises. E asks for compact and renew through this contract and receives capability-insufficient or failure receipts with the old and new generation; E never builds vendor-private commands. Admission is one boundary for E's cap, F's concurrency and H's launch.

Cursor and epoch, duplicate and gap semantics, reader scope checked on every read; the global store has no path from project scope. The side chat's own turns are recorded here in the side-chat tier; its registry is K-SIDE's store; deleting a side chat removes its tier entries and never touches the lead's.

messageId plus revision; target is seat plus turn plus generation; edit and cancel race by revision; delivery is committed through H's existing prepare, beginCommitted, completion chain with the current grant rechecked; delivered only with a receipt; the UNKNOWN check never writes.

Bound to request, seat and turn; options with one recommended and a free answer; duplicate answers rejected; native cards passed through, ours used where the capability report shows none. The own-card path is settled at M2 with a real vendor that has no native card.
Registry persisted in D's native store in the same coordination domain; source ledger cursor; permission tier and caller; native fork only if behaviour-equivalent to ledger replay.

Layer check on every call: the lead touches lead-layer seats only, inside user-set bounds, never its own binding. Instance change on a busy seat is refused. E.1 settles registry and binding at M1; the rest at M2.
Trusted sender from the host's issuer boundary, never self-declared by Node or the model. Secretary triggers live in the existing coordinator with de-duplication; they are settled at M3 with E.3.

Instance home persistent, per-session and per-call directories temporary, vendor memory off, credentials never read. F.1 settles registry, home and login state at M1; versions, re-pin and concurrency at M2.
Merge only by a seat granted merge permission, decision and reason recorded; cleanup only after the stop fact with no active admission reservation, never by directory name alone.

Every read model and action maps to an operation of the contracts above with its receipt; G adds no operation or state source of its own; every A1-A4 state has a read model, including unknown and unconfirmed states.

checks.observe: Every K-* suite passes on its fake. The listed contracts pass the same cases on the real implementation delivered by M1, limited to the families that the M1 phases deliver; records written before the v37 schema are still decoded; each shared-file extension point used so far is exercised through the product entry.
The listed contracts pass the same cases on the real implementations delivered by M2, including the remaining families of K-SEAT, K-INSTANCE and K-SESSION and the own-card path of K-QCARD.
All ten contracts pass on the installed candidate's real implementations.

A pinned Codex binary started by the host from the product entry; raw and normalised events, stop fact and restart reconciliation in the ledger with no loss and no duplicate; unconfirmed input reconciled, not resent.

On a real seat: edit and cancel race by revision; no delivered without receipt; turn-end keeps the message queued; delivered cannot be edited; UNKNOWN check performs no write; cancel and failure keep records; requeue makes a new message; interrupt-and-resume is disclosed in the receipt. The focus rule and disabled actions per state are settled in V15.
A native Codex question passed through and answered; answer bound to request, seat and turn; duplicate and expired answers rejected; recovery after disconnect.

For each real vendor whose capability report shows no native question card, our card is raised with a recommended option and a free answer, and the answer reaches the asking turn; if every vendor has a native card, this check is NOT_RUN with that reason, never PASS.

Codex instance home is separate from the Owner's everyday home (launch configuration and file-access record); the host never opens credential files; the effective launch configuration has vendor memory off; the Codex memory store inside the instance home is not created or written across two sessions.

Per vendor at its pinned version: effective memory-off configuration and no write to the vendor's memory store; the same instance serving two projects at once, where a synthetic marker given in project A is absent from the actual input record of a new session in project B; instruction files outside the workspace are not loaded. Behaviour a vendor cannot support is recorded as NOT_RUN with the reason; startup success is never promoted to isolation evidence.

Each of the other four CLIs at a pinned version, started by the host from the product entry: open, resume, steer or disclosed interrupt-and-resume, stop fact; capability report matches the measured behaviour. No CLI is inferred from another.

Lead creates seats from a template, tunes the copy and the template and another project stay unchanged; the user layer adjusts and reclaims lead-layer seats; refusals when the lead exceeds bounds, touches user-layer seats, changes its own binding or creates recursively; busy seat cannot change instance; switching never double-dispatches; short to long; reclaim refused when the lead's conditions are unmet; reclaimed ledger readable; the parallel cap from machine resources holds under load.
No new work into an overlapping workspace until the stop fact, including a leftover child process and a host restart; worktree cleanup waits for the same fact.

Positive: approve and reject-with-reason recorded, a legal stage transition recorded, each traceable in the ledger. Negative: rejections recorded for a forged sender, a cross-project call, a bypassed configured gate, a subordinate seat addressing the Owner and an expired grant; reject cap escalates; a stalled seat escalates along the configured chain without an Owner popup.

Dispatch refused until every takeover question from the configured template has an answer with a cited source or an explicit unknown with a way to find out; host-provided space facts offered as options; answers stored in the state card and restored after restart.

Synthetic markers, per vendor: a formal review session in the same seat after a side chat receives none of the side-chat or lead-private material (actual input record and native session identity), and resume or fork into it is refused; a worker in the same project cannot read Owner-lead conversation; project-scope retrieval has no path to the global store; distribution from global is explicit and cited. Model self-report is not evidence; unsupported vendor behaviour is NOT_RUN.

Writes land only in host-created worktrees; a direct write to the main tree is refused; a vendor-native worktree attempt outside the space is blocked; a read-only or no-network tier the host cannot guarantee is refused or shown as unavailable, never passed on a weaker statement; single and mixed trees stored apart, including one repository serving two projects; the graph answers origin, users and merge target; merge only by the permitted seat with reason recorded; commits carry project, seat, instance and turn; push credentials never read.

Zero model calls on open and on sync (provider call record); pending deltas attached to the next question, or appended where supported; on-demand read of this project's threads only; a reference asks to change a file inside the side chat's own writable worktree and, without a new explicit Owner request, no tool call happens and the file hash is unchanged; with an explicit request the write succeeds; a kept side chat reopens after restart; archive then restore works; lead context is referenced by cursor, not stored twice; delete leaves the lead ledger byte-identical.

Automatic compaction and session renewal from health signals through K-SESSION with a low-key record and no Owner prompt; install guidance for the pinned version; concurrency cap enforced; new version shown and never auto-upgraded; after the Owner's manual upgrade the program identity is re-pinned and capabilities re-probed; a CLI-reported exhaustion or error, injected at the real CLI boundary without spending real quota, marks affected seats and no instance changes silently.

Secretary seat reads all projects' live events, delivers to a lead and an auditor, runs a scheduled trigger that survives a restart without firing twice, and the content it sends into a project is filtered to that project's scope, judged from the delivered content, not the secretary's statement.

From the installed candidate, each of the 25 appendix-A states is driven by a real action or a fault injected at the real boundary and is visible in the real UI, including unknown and unconfirmed states; in each state the actions the design disallows are disabled and recovery works; the recipient never changes on focus change; any state not reached is NOT_RUN and the check cannot PASS; the style check finds no literal colours, new fonts, new radii or new spacing values.

Exact source, installer and CLI versions and hashes; cloud run and job ids; executed, failed, skipped and NOT_RUN recorded separately; each new executable component observed on the Owner's Win11 with Smart App Control on; a per-check provenance table shows, for V00a-V15, which result was produced on this candidate and which was carried over under the carry-over rule.

evidence_carryover.rule: Every check result is bound to the source commit and the hashes of the components it exercised. At M3 a result from M1 or M2 carries over to the candidate only when every exercised component and its configuration are byte-identical on the candidate; otherwise the check is re-run on the candidate. V16 publishes the per-check provenance table.
